stem: An axe blade or a knife's cutting edge, which is essentially two inclined planes joined back-to-back, concentrates force into a narrow edge to split or cut material. This simple machine is called a:
explanation: A wedge is formed by two inclined planes joined at their base, moving through material to split it apart (as in an axe, knife, or doorstop) — one of the six classical simple machines alongside the lever, wheel and axle, pulley, inclined plane, and screw.
